title: A Supply Chain Attack Put Malicious Anthropic Claude Extensions on Thousands of Devices
gist: A backdoored copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension sat in the IDE extension marketplace of Cursor (owned by SpaceX) for about 11 hours and was downloaded by at most 5,000 users. A design flaw kept the malware from fully installing on most machines. Anthropic says its own systems were not compromised and that someone used access to Cursor's marketplace, while how the upload happened remains unexplained.

themes.theme: Malicious extension in the Cursor marketplace

insights.claim: A malicious Claude Code extension for Windows, macOS and Linux was live in Cursor's IDE extension marketplace for roughly 11 hours and was downloaded by at most 5,000 users. Cursor briefly shut down the marketplace and published remediation steps.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Extension marketplaces for AI coding tools are now a real supply-chain attack vector into developer machines.
insights.quote: The company says the rogue extension was downloaded by “at most 5,000 users.”

insights.claim: The tainted extension carried a backdoor, the kind of implant attackers use as a stepping stone to deeper network control, but a flaw in its design kept it from fully establishing itself on most targets.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: The impact this time was limited by luck, not defenses, so a better-built version could do serious damage.
insights.quote: A saving grace of the situation, though, was a flaw in the malware's design that blocked it from fully establishing itself on the vast majority of targets.

insights.claim: Anthropic's Felix Rieseberg said Anthropic's systems and employee laptops were not compromised. He said a malicious actor used access to Cursor's marketplace to publish a tampered copy of the Claude Code extension, and that Anthropic's official channels are unaffected.
insights.speaker: Felix Rieseberg
insights.so_what: Responsibility points to the marketplace operator rather than the publisher of the original extension.

insights.so_what: Unanswered questions about how the upload got in leave Cursor's marketplace security in doubt.
